display_title: Ten Hag Criticizes Ronaldo and United
display_title_he: טן האך מבקר את רונאלדו ומנצ'סטר יונייטד
short_summary: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has criticized Cristiano Ronaldo and the club's hierarchy, while current coach Michael Carrick insists he retains the board's full backing.

sources.name: BBC Sport
sources.title: Ronaldo let Manchester United down - Ten Hag

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: Carrick insists Manchester United board back him after Ten Hag points to ‘toxic culture’

paragraphs: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has opened up about his turbulent spell at Old Trafford, launching sharp criticisms directed at both Portuguese superstar Cristiano Ronaldo and the club's executive leadership. According to recent interviews, Ten Hag asserted that Ronaldo let the team down significantly during his second stint at the club. The Dutch manager explained that he had traveled to Portugal to plan the team's future around the forward, whom he deeply respected as one of history's greatest players. However, Ten Hag claimed that rational decisions had to be made because Ronaldo failed to prepare himself adequately for the rigorous physical demands of modern football, refusing to press opponents or run properly in and out of possession. He noted that the forward could not run because he was not properly prepared, even telling other players to save their legs during training sessions.

Beyond his remarks regarding Ronaldo—who recently received a thirty-day suspension and a two hundred and fifty-five euro fine from the Portuguese Football Federation—Ten Hag did not hold back in criticizing the Manchester United hierarchy. He alleged that the club's management fostered a toxic culture that continued to fuel issues and gave too much power to the players. Furthermore, Ten Hag accused the board of breaking promises made during talks that led to him agreeing a contract extension, specifically pointing to the sale of Scott McTominay to Napoli in August 2024, a move he had strongly opposed. The former manager, who was sacked in October 2024 after winning the Carabao Cup in 2023 and the FA Cup in 2024, also mentioned that he wanted to sign players like Frenkie de Jong, Harry Kane, and Declan Rice to solve the team's ongoing goalscoring issues during his tenure.

Meanwhile, current head coach Michael Carrick has firmly defended the club's leadership as his squad prepares for an upcoming Champions League fixture against Como. Addressing reporters, Carrick insisted that he enjoys a strong, healthy relationship with everyone in the executive branch, including the chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, and does not require any special reassurances about his job security. This comes despite a disappointing run of six matches without a victory across all competitions, which leaves United thirteenth in the Premier League following a one-all draw at Leeds. Carrick explicitly denied experiencing any toxic culture within the club, praising the unwavering dedication of his current players and staff.

However, Carrick faces a daunting challenge ahead of the match in Italy, as he must cope with a severe injury and suspension crisis. With as many as nine players unavailable—including several frontline defenders such as Leny Yoro, who is suspended, Ayden Heaven, who is ill, alongside injured players Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu, and Manuel Ugarte—the manager is forced to assemble an unfamiliar defensive line. This experimental setup may feature Matthijs de Ligt returning from a long-term back problem or a potential appearance for nineteen-year-old left-back Harry Amass, with a severe weather warning for lightning and rain also looming over the fixture in Como.

facts.fact: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag stated in an interview that Cristiano Ronaldo 'let the team and let me down' during their time together at Old Trafford.
Ten Hag criticized Ronaldo's physical preparation and pressing ability, stating the forward did not run in or out of possession.
Ten Hag also expressed frustration with the club's hierarchy, claiming broken promises and pointing to a 'toxic culture' that empowers players, citing the sale of Scott McTominay against his wishes.

Current Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick defended the club's board, stating he has a good relationship with everyone and does not need reassurance despite a run of six games without a win.
Carrick's side prepares to face Como in the Champions League amid an extensive injury and suspension crisis affecting several frontline defenders.
